clue.text: Strip tease imitation?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to remove clothing, as a phrasal verb

definitions.note: the answer read as one noun, a take-off
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a mocking impersonation of someone

explanation.surface: A burlesque act is dismissed as a poor copy of the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip tease' looks like one word; split it, and 'Strip' is one meaning while 'tease imitation' is the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off clothes is to strip, and a take-off is a parody that mocks its target.

clue.text: Worked on the books, also took first place

parts.note: a plain synonym
to lead a race is to be in first place

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper who also topped the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked on the books' suggests accounting, but it means decorating leather bindings with heated tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookbinders tool leather covers, pressing decorative patterns and gilt lettering into them with heated hand tools.

clue.text: Cape Kennedy's opening can provide joint cover

indicators.note: the letters are made to supply something new, so they are rearranged into another word

parts.note: taken as written
the opening three letters of the surname

explanation.surface: The launch site at Cape Kennedy offers shelter for some structure.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Kennedy was the name of Cape Canaveral, Florida, from 1963 to 1973; only its first three letters join the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the small bone protecting the front of the knee joint, so it literally covers a joint.

clue.text: Astronomical number the Italian brightened the company up with

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means these words are read from the bottom, in the opposite direction

parts.note: il is the Italian word for the
lit up, made bright
the usual abbreviation for company
to be on with someone is to be with them

explanation.surface: An Italian livened up the party with a huge figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first three pieces are turned round; ON is added after them.
explanation.definitionFit: An octillion is a vast figure, ten to the twenty-seventh power, the sort of size met in astronomy.

clue.text: Game birds obstruct the hunter

parts.note: surface reading: pheasants or grouse getting in a shooter's way; setter's reading: a board game in which the birds try to hem in a predator

explanation.surface: Pheasants get in the way of a man with a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game birds' reads as one phrase; split it, 'Game' names the answer's category and the rest describes how it is played.
explanation.definitionFit: In this old board game many pieces, the geese, try to trap a single fox piece so it cannot move.

clue.text: It's real in the form of a cross

indicators.note: the letters are recast into another shape, which means rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cross-shaped thing is claimed to be genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal X-shaped cross, as on the Scottish flag of St Andrew.

clue.text: For some sob-sisters, a description?

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the letters sit inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the second word, the a, and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A word to sum up weepy agony-aunt journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: Sob-sisters were journalists who wrote sentimental stories; the whole clue is both the definition and the place the letters hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of tear-jerking stories deal in sorrow, so unhappy or mournful is a fitting label for them.

clue.text: Singers on the way up

parts.note: surface reading: performers whose careers are rising; setter's reading: songbirds famous for singing as they climb into the sky

explanation.surface: Rising pop stars climbing the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Skylarks pour out song while ascending high above fields, so they are literally birds singing as they go upward.

clue.text: Prepare to send the economic balloon up?

definitions.text: Prepare to send the economic balloon up?

parts.note: surface reading: filling a balloon with air before letting it go; setter's reading: making prices rise across an economy

explanation.surface: Getting a balloon ready for launch.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump up a balloon or to drive up an economy's prices and money supply are both expressed by this verb.

clue.text: Lear's daughter had one on a string

parts.words: Lear's daughter had one on a string
parts.note: surface reading: King Lear's daughter keeping a suitor dangling; setter's reading: Cordelia's name, a string of letters, ends with a famous pen name, Elia

explanation.surface: One of King Lear's daughters keeps a lover dangling.
explanation.walkthrough: Elia was the pen name of Charles Lamb, the English writer of short prose pieces; it sits at the end of CORDELIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb, writing as Elia, was a celebrated composer of short prose pieces, so 'one' refers to such a writer.

clue.text: Apparent cut-down (so expect a refund)

definitions.note: describes the state of having paid too much tax; the answer is an adjective

parts.note: plain to see
chopped down, as a tree

explanation.surface: A visible budget cut, with a refund promised.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone charged more tax than is owed will be due money back from the revenue office.

clue.text: Birds as a guide to the horses

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wading birds of the sandpiper family

definitions.note: the answer here is a title, Ruff's Guide
definitions.meaning: second meaning: ... Guide to the Turf, a long-running British annual of horse-racing records

explanation.surface: Watching birds as a way to pick a winning racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruff's Guide to the Turf was a British horse-racing reference book published yearly from the 1840s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffs are sandpipers whose males grow showy neck feathers, and the racing annual carried this possessive name.

clue.text: What Silvia would do in Rome at forty, say?

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the item aloud and use the word it sounds like

parts.note: forty in Roman numerals is X followed by L

explanation.surface: Wondering how a woman would perform in Rome when forty.
explanation.walkthrough: Silvia is from Shakespeare's song 'Who is Silvia?' in The Two Gentlemen of Verona: 'She excels each mortal thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: The song says Silvia surpasses every mortal creature on earth, so outdoing all others is her action.

clue.text: It must be the 24

definitions.note: paraphrases the adjective: something that must be is needed
24 across is READY; 'the ready' and 'the necessary' are both slang for money
definitions.meaning: second meaning: cash, since the ready is money in hand

explanation.walkthrough: 'The necessary' is old British slang for money, the same as 'the ready' at 24 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Something required cannot be avoided, and in British slang 'the necessary' means funds, just like 'the ready'.

clue.text: Drivers causing a riot amid applause

indicators.note: amid places one thing in the middle of another, so one set of words goes inside the other

parts.note: shouts of approval
taken as written

explanation.surface: Motorists stir up trouble while a crowd cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: Charioteers drove horse-drawn chariots in ancient races, so they are drivers in the oldest sense.

clue.text: But it's a good lie, what, ever the season

definitions.text: But it's a good lie, what, ever the season

parts.words: it's a good lie, what, ever the season
parts.note: surface reading: an untruth that works well; setter's reading: a comfortable thing to lie on, named after a season of the year

explanation.surface: Defending a fib as useful at any time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' means lying down, not telling an untruth; the season named in the answer is spring, though the bed is good all year.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress with coiled metal springs inside gives a comfortable place to sleep, whatever the weather.

clue.text: Incisive worker in World War I?

parts.note: WWI soldiers fought from long dug-out ditches
a worker is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: A sharp-minded labourer serving in the Great War.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant remarks are sharp and cutting, keen and forceful in a way that cuts to the point.

clue.text: The joiner who made Queen Mah's chariot

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a carpenter commissioned for a royal coach
setter's reading: in Romeo and Juliet, Mercutio says Queen Mab's chariot is a hazelnut shell made by a woodland creature

explanation.surface: Naming the carpenter who built a fairy queen's coach.
explanation.walkthrough: Mah is a misprint for Mab, the fairy queen of Mercutio's speech: 'Her chariot is an empty hazel-nut, Made by the joiner squirrel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare names a bushy-tailed nut-gnawing rodent as the craftsman, since it hollows out hazelnuts.

clue.text: As a sequence even I'd arrange to turn this

definitions.note: the answer completes the phrase 'turn queen's evidence'

indicators.note: to arrange is to put things into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tidies an ordered list of even numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a criminal who turns Queen's evidence testifies against accomplices in return for leniency.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn Queen's evidence is to become a prosecution witness against one's former partners in crime.

clue.text: Once a miner's piece of land, I do declare!

definitions.note: an example of the cry the verb describes

parts.note: ex means former
a plot staked out by a prospector

explanation.surface: An old prospector's plot prompts a cry of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying out 'I do declare!' is a typical exclamation, a sudden outburst of surprise uttered aloud.

clue.text: Gel one's opponent's at breaking-point in the game, say

definitions.note: probably a misprint for 'Get one's opponent's'; the answer means beat

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the item and take the word with that sound

parts.note: the horse-chestnut used in the schoolyard game of conkers

explanation.surface: Getting an opponent's conker to snap in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Conkers is a British children's game: horse chestnuts on strings are swung to smash the other player's nut.
explanation.definitionFit: To defeat someone is to break their resistance, just as winning at conkers means smashing the rival chestnut.

clue.text: "That unhoped —, That men call age" (Brooke)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Rupert Brooke's sonnet Menelaus and Helen, where the missing word is used as a noun for calm old age

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a gap-fill: complete the Brooke line. In 'Menelaus and Helen' the aged Menelaus and Helen reach 'the unhoped serene, That men call age', using the adjective as a poetic noun meaning calm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means calm and untroubled, and Brooke uses it as a noun for the tranquil state of old age.

clue.text: Could the parson, for instance, be lying?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the holder of a church office

definitions.note: the answer as an adjective, from the Latin for lying upon
definitions.meaning: second meaning: resting or leaning on something, a literal sense

explanation.surface: Asking whether a vicar might be telling fibs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' is not telling untruths; it is the posture, as in lying on top of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson holds a church benefice as its office-holder, and the Latin root incumbere means to lie or lean upon.

clue.text: What Roy early to rise can become

definitions.text: What Roy early to rise can become

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading these letters from the bottom upward

parts.note: taken as written
a.m., the morning hours

explanation.surface: An early-rising man called Roy could become a civic leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the familiar proverb says early rising leads to success, here public office.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ambitious and early to rise might end up as head of a town council, wearing the chain of office.

clue.text: Leave this reel for the fish

definitions.meaning: the definition: formal dismissal or permission to depart
setter's reading: put the answer in front of the word reel and you get a kind of sea fish

explanation.surface: Abandoning a fishing reel meant for the catch.
explanation.walkthrough: Add REEL after the answer and it reads CONGER EEL, a large sea fish; 'reel' is not tackle at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Congé, borrowed from French, means dismissal or formal permission to go, as in being given one's leave.

clue.text: The cash in hand?

definitions.note: 'the ready' is a noun for money, so the clue's article belongs to the phrase rather than being a link
definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for money available at once

definitions.note: a prepositional phrase defining an adjective, fair because both describe something prepared and available for use
definitions.meaning: second meaning: prepared, available to use

explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' is British slang for cash, short for ready money.
explanation.definitionFit: Money one holds for immediate use is ready money, and something in hand is prepared for use.

clue.text: Too early, like the minority

definitions.meaning: first meaning: before the proper time

definitions.note: a cryptic sense: pre-mature, not yet grown up
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as before maturity, the condition of minors under legal age

explanation.surface: Something happening too soon, as with the smaller group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minority' suggests the smaller group; here it means being under age, a minor.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming before the due time is untimely, and minors are literally at the stage before adulthood.

clue.text: Make regular journeys in the Strand?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to travel a route back and forth, as a ferry does
second meaning: a single twisted thread of yarn or rope

explanation.surface: A bus or cab running up and down a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a famous London street, which is the false trail; the capital letter hides a thread of rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferries ply between ports on a fixed route, and a three-ply rope or wool has three twisted threads.

clue.text: The fish to beat its victim

parts.note: to lam is to thrash
an animal hunted for food

explanation.surface: A fish sets out to strike whatever it hunts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lampreys are jawless eel-like aquatic creatures that clamp onto other fish with sucker mouths.

clue.text: The present radio release?

parts.note: a radio receiver is a set
a present is given free

explanation.surface: A wireless given as a gift is about to be launched.
explanation.walkthrough: A present radio is a free set; the words go into the grid in the order set then free.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate a prisoner or a caged animal is to let it go, to release it from captivity.
